status: BOUNDED EXTERNAL PASS COMPLETE — source-level technical concordance
research_question: How did nineteenth-century microscopists convert an exact microscopic field or object into an address that could survive displacement across time, operators, instruments, media, and collections?
scope_guard: Satellite project only. This concordance does not reopen the frozen 307/155 microscope-slide survey or the parked repository bibliography.

mechanism_families.name: instrument_or_stage_bound_coordinate_frame
mechanism_families.definition: A numerical or geometrical address is generated by the microscope stage, mechanical carrier, or a reference frame whose validity depends on repeatable instrument geometry.
mechanism_families.typical_strength: direct numerical return on a calibrated setup
mechanism_families.typical_failure: address degrades if stage/instrument relation, zero, orientation, carrier geometry, or calibration changes

mechanism_families.name: transferable_external_indicator_or_carrier
mechanism_families.definition: A separate indicator/card/carrier externalizes the spatial relation so that the recorded location is not restricted to the original microscope.
mechanism_families.typical_strength: designed for correspondence and inter-observer transfer
mechanism_families.typical_failure: requires a stable convention for aligning the indicator with the preparation

mechanism_families.name: substitution_reference_slide_or_grid
mechanism_families.definition: The preparation is replaced at a reproducible stage position by a ruled/photographic reference slide; the reference read at the same optical point becomes the address of the target.
mechanism_families.typical_strength: portable address can travel with the recorded reference rather than the original microscope
mechanism_families.typical_failure: depends on repeatable slide orientation, edge geometry, stop/contact relation, and grid convention

mechanism_families.name: direct_material_target_marking
mechanism_families.definition: The target position is materially marked on the coverslip, slide, or preparation layer, for example by a diamond or steel point producing a ring around the desired locality.
mechanism_families.typical_strength: reference remains on the preparation itself and needs no numerical coordinate transform
mechanism_families.typical_failure: physical modification can damage, obscure, or be separated from the preparation; mark precision is finite

mechanism_families.name: optical_or_eyepiece_transfer_reference
mechanism_families.definition: An optical reference in the eyepiece or optical train is used to preserve or transfer locality, including across changes of objective or magnification.
mechanism_families.typical_strength: can transfer a locality through changes in optical configuration
mechanism_families.typical_failure: reference remains dependent on optical alignment and instrument configuration

mechanism_families.name: within_slide_spatial_index_comparator
mechanism_families.definition: A slide contains several named/numbered specimen positions but does not necessarily encode arbitrary field relocation.

mechanism_families.name: reference_object_repeatability_comparator
mechanism_families.definition: A stable test object or calibrated surface makes a comparison repeatable rather than relocating an arbitrary microscopic locality.
mechanism_families.core_status: orthogonal comparator; keep outside finder core

cross_case_findings: The important chronology is not invention of one finder but coexistence and competition among reference frames from the early 1850s onward.
Bailey 1855 is the strongest early conceptual articulation of portability: the address should remain useful away from the original microscope and observer and support correspondence/interchange.
Maltwood's importance lies in a substitution-grid architecture that converts stable slide placement into a portable reference address.
Direct material marking is not a late alternative: Bridgman already places it in the mid-1850s, contemporaneous with early coordinate/indicator systems.
The Bailey Collection provides rare object-level evidence of re-addressing from Bailey's Indicator regime to later Maltwood Finder references.
By the 1880s 'finder' names several distinct operations: stage/carrier coordinates, substitution grids, eyepiece transfer, bacteriological frames, and physical marking.
Klein/Winkel connects relocation to selection from mixed microscopic material: selection and marking can be part of making an individual microscopic form into a durable research object.
Grunow shows that relocation can be cross-media: coordinate, exact valve, drawing, and work-status record form one operational chain.
The central historical variable is what part of the reference frame survives displacement of slide, stage, microscope, magnification, operator, or time.

evidence_scale.S: source/object chain under strong direct control; suitable as central case
evidence_scale.B: historically secure and mechanism broadly controlled, but exact primary description or figure remains incomplete
